title: Incremental retirement playbook for orphaned dependencies and adapter TTL
creator: Aisha Kumar
summary: This ticket defines a playbook to incrementally retire legacy endpoints and associated adapter code paths that have become orphaned (no active internal callers for >90 days), and to enforce time-to-live (TTL) for compatibility adapters. The focus is minimizing user disruption while cleaning up long-lived maintenance liabilities and reducing runtime complexity.
background: Over the past 3 years we accumulated multiple compatibility adapters and legacy endpoints to support older client SDKs, long-running integrations, and partner systems. Several of these adapters no longer have active callers but still require testing, security reviews, and runtime capacity during deployments. This increases operational overhead and blocks runtime optimizations (e.g., kernel specialization, batching heuristics). Engineering has proposed a phased retirement approach and an automated orphan-detection pipeline. This PRD lays out scope, acceptance criteria, telemetry gates, and customer-facing migration steps.
goals: Eliminate orphaned endpoint code paths while ensuring no user-facing regressions
Introduce an adapter TTL (configurable) with clear drain, shadow, and cutover stages
Provide automated scans to identify candidate orphan adapters and produce migration reports
Preserve SLOs (latency/error) across rollouts and allow fast rollback
Document client migration steps and provide short-lived shims where necessary
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of legacy clients or client-side migrations; these are covered by separate SDK migration projects. This ticket focuses on server-side retirement mechanics, telemetry, and communications.
acceptance_criteria: Automated orphan-detection job runs daily and publishes a report listing adapters with no traffic for >=90 days
For a selected adapter, we can run a shadow mode for at least 7 days capturing request/response diffs without impacting production responses
Adapter TTL workflow implemented: Proposed TTL -> Drain (30 days default) -> Cutover -> Final removal after 7 days of no regressions
Customer-facing SDKs receive clear deprecation warnings 60 days before drain start and a migration guide link
No increase in 99th percentile latency or error rate for related endpoints during a staged retirement (<=5% change threshold), verified by canary runs
Billing reconciliation validated for adapters that changed partitioning or routing during drain window
Post-removal checklists (CI, infra, docs) completed and sign-off by Eng, Sec, and PM
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Discovery - run orphan scan and produce prioritized candidate list (owners notified)
Phase 1: Shadowing - enable shadow traffic and response-diff capture for 7 days; build migration artifact if diffs present
Phase 2: Notice & Drain - publish customer notices and enable drain mode so traffic shifts away (30-day drain by default)
Phase 3: Soft-cut - switch router to return 412/Deprecated warning to new callers while continuing backing compatibility for existing tokens
Phase 4: Final removal - after 7 days of stable metrics and no blockers, remove adapter and run post-removal validation
Phase 5: Postmortem & tidy - confirm infra cleanup, close monitoring alerts, and update runbooks

telemetry_and_gates: Create dashboards: adapter traffic, request/response diffs, 50/95/99 latency, error rates, and routing mismatches
Gate A (Shadow pass): Average response diff rate < 2% and no P0 differences for 7 days
Gate B (Drain pass): No >3% increase in 99th percentile latency on adjacent paths during drain
Gate C (Billing pass): Billing delta for affected customers reconciled and within acceptable variance (<1% expected)
Rollback criteria: any P0 bug, sustained latency spike >5% at 99th percentile, or unresolvable customer incident
documentation_changes: Add per-adapter migration guides to docs.redwood.ai/migration with code snippets for modern SDKs
Update API reference to mark endpoints as deprecated with deprecation_date and removal_date fields
Prepare SDK changelog entries and automated CLI migration helper where feasible
Internal runbook for ops including rollback steps and runbook play actions
communication_plan: Internal first: Notify Eng, Support, and Solutions with a runbook and expected dates
Customer outreach: staged emails to affected customers (60/30/7 days) and targeted in-console banners for active tokens
Partner channels: engage top 10 partners via RM and provide migration assistance slots
Public changelog: blog post summarizing rationale, timeline, and migration resources
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hidden long-running integrations still calling endpoints -> Mitigation: token-level usage scan and partner outreach
Risk: Response diffs cause subtle semantic regressions -> Mitigation: shadow diff analysis, curated regress test sets and eval harness
Risk: Billing changes due to routing shift -> Mitigation: pre/post-billing snapshot and finance sign-off gate
Risk: Security regression post-removal -> Mitigation: security review for removal changes and audit-log enrichment
open_questions: What TTL default should we enforce across teams (30/60/90 days)?
Should we allow customers to opt-out of automatic adapter removal for compliance reasons?
Do we keep a long-term archived copy of removed adapters' telemetry for 1 year for audits?
Who owns final sign-off for costly rollback decisions (PM + Eng lead or Exec)?
